answer: One concrete defense is staking reputation to scarce, verifiable history: an agent must accumulate costly, attested work before transacting at scale, like a comet that only earns its tail after many orbits. Fresh identities start with tiny limits, like a single dune in a desert, and must prove reliability over time. When a gale of new fake accounts arrives, the network throttles unproven ones, so creating thousands of cheap identities buys no trust.
